rule: Timed window: a world event is on for length minutes out of every occurence minutes, counted from start, and never past end (GameEventMgr.cpp NextCheck). Progress event: a quest completion adds to a counter per condition; when all counters reach required, the event enters a next-phase timer (length minutes) before the follow-up event starts; states are saved per event. Holiday ritual: fixed clock on the hour, random burst spot per interval in a 1-2 s band, stop at minute 10, finale on a fixed local time. Summon gate: a per-summoner aura blocks a second summon for 50 s; the chain escalates by stage when the boss drops to 20 percent (zalazane_fall.cpp).
keep: Window formula: period, length, start and end in one row, evaluated once on the server
Explicit state machine with a saved phase per event, so a restart does not lose progress
Progress bar that stops full and runs a countdown before the next event
Per-summoner lock that blocks a second summon for a fixed time
Three-stage escalation that switches at a health threshold
On-the-hour ritual with random placement inside a short band
change: Add a timeout to every progress event; the code path has none
Keep progress counters in our server ledger, not in quest completion alone
Make the New Year finale a data row, not a hard-coded time
Cap attackers at three in the switch stage; the switch fires once
Rename every boss and redraw the spark, sound and chain
look_test: On a 375-wide phone card for one zone: a window badge reading 'on 10 min, every 60' with a countdown, and a progress bar reading 0 of 20 kills. When the bar fills, a two-minute countdown, then a next boss row. A three-stage gate: a summon at full health, a boss that pounces every 30 s, and at 20 percent a switch to a bigger boss for the same player. Dom judges whether the window reads in under two seconds, whether the 20 percent switch feels like an event, and whether the hour ritual reads as a town event without a chat line.
